report:
Reviewed the complete claim, sole ordinary implementation association in local_syms/mods.rs, both ordinary harness tests and the semantic_spec TODO. Independently verified exact byte equality of all three current source files against the supplied historical input; the previous rationale remains applicable, with the qualifications below.

The claim separates safe positive publication from exhaustive negative conclusions and makes completeness question-specific. local_expanded_module_items retains represented ordinary items and successful recursive expansion output. Error entries are omitted; unresolved bang macros and depth-limited expansion do not publish invented items; active-attribute inputs are withheld because transformation could replace them. bang_macro_expansion_complete independently rejects unresolved definitions, parse errors, active attributes and the depth limit, recursively examining nested output. Trait-specific completeness checks derive relevance to the target trait; method-provider and symbol-listing policies differ appropriately, with symbol listing requiring represented derive output and provider discovery rejecting arbitrary procedural output. Thus omission alone is not the completeness certificate.

The two full ordinary test bodies construct ground bool: Marker goals without assumptions and explicitly assert QueryResultData::Maybe for missing!() and malformed impl output. These assertions detect the relevant false-negative failure, and normal test completion also excludes the malformed-output panic. Captured trait_and_crate helper finds Marker among expanded items: both fixtures therefore additionally exercise continued publication of an unaffected known trait during incomplete expansion. Captured fixture helpers install the literal source and invoke the callback with a root module. These tests do not establish the whole matrix or universal safe-positive behavior.

The explicit TODO modules_expand_completeness retains the missing successful-expansion ground-negative comparison and unsupported/resource-limited uncertainty matrix; it is an empty placeholder, not executed behavioral evidence. Its prerequisite is a claim-specific set of fixtures and visible query assertions contrasting complete expansion with each incomplete outcome, including depth exhaustion and unsupported transformations, while checking retained positive symbols. Existing malformed/unresolved examples partially satisfy that matrix but do not retire the TODO. This remains an accepted verification deferral, not a claim of complete implementation/test coverage. No N/A entries exist and no source edits are requested.

Method: source inspection and exact historical comparison, with additional review-policy and test-helper dependencies captured through review read. I ran review start/read and byte-comparison commands, and record this report myself; I did not run behavioral tests or a workspace build. The coordinator-reported 321 sage-meta tests and cargo build are separate baseline execution evidence, not execution of these harness tests by this reviewer.
